  CITY OF SANTA MONICA

  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES

  DECEMBER 29, 2020

  A special meeting of the Santa Monica City Council was called to order by Mayor Himmelrich at 3:01 p.m.,
  on Tuesday, December 29, 2020, via teleconference pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Order N-29-20 at
  https://primetime.bluejeans.com/a2m/live-event/tkpwgjzq

  Roll Call:  Present:  Mayor Sue Himmelrich
  Mayor Pro Tem Kristin McCowan
  Councilmember Phil Brock
  Councilmember Gleam Davis (arrived at 3:06 p.m.)
  Councilmember Oscar de la Torre (arrived at 3:03 p.m.)
  Councilmember Kevin McKeown
  Councilmember Christine Parra

  Also Present:  Interim City Manager Lane Dilg
  Interim City Attorney George Cardona
  City Clerk Denise Anderson-Warren

  CONVENE  On order of the Mayor, the City Council convened at 3:01 p.m., with all
  members present except Councilmembers De la Torre and Davis.

  CLOSED SESSIONS  Members of the public Denise Barton and Olga Zurawska commented on
  closed sessions.
  Councilmember De la Torre
  arrived at 3:03 p.m.  The City Attorney announced that with respect to Item 1.A, staff was
  planning a very limited discussion with Council that would be permissible
  Councilmember Davis  under the Brown Act. In light of the many emails, some of which threaten
  arrived at 3:06 p.m.  litigation, however, staff is simply pulling this item from the agenda. Staff
  will instead be returning with a series of open and closed session items
  relating to the recruitment that we will be scheduled for future Council
  meetings.

  On order of the Mayor, the City Council recessed at 3:12 p.m., to consider
  closed sessions and returned at 5:04 p.m., with all members present, to
  report the following:

  1.A. Public Employee Appointment, Government Code Section
  54957(b): Recruitment of City Manager.

  1  December 29, 2020
 DocuSign Envelope ID: 03AEE48F-7A3E-4B58-A069-4BC128206EF7

  This item was pulled at the request of staff, and not heard.

  1B. Conference with Legal Counsel –Anticipated Litigation –
  Anticipate significant exposure to litigation pursuant to Government
  Code Section 54956.9(d)(2): Threat of Litigation by Olga Zurawska
  relating to alleged Brown Act violation in connection with the selection
  of the Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem at the December 8, 2020 Council
  meeting.

  The Interim City Attorney advised this matter was heard with no reportable
  action taken.

  1.C. Conference with Legal Counsel –Anticipated Litigation –
  Anticipate significant exposure to litigation pursuant to Government
  Code Section 54956.9(d)(2): Threat of litigation by Santa Monica
  Police Officers Association relating to City’s denial of grievance
  seeking overtime pay for Lieutenants and Captains for the period
  5/30/2020 to 6/13/2020.

  The Interim City Attorney advised Items 1.C. and 1.D. were heard together.

  The Interim City Attorney reported that the Santa Monica Police Officers’
  Association, on behalf of a group of Captains and Lieutenants, has filed
  with the City a claim seeking overtime compensation for hours worked
  between May 30, 2020 and June 13, 2020, alleging that they are entitled to
  this overtime compensation under Section 2.03 of the SMPOA
  Memorandum of Understanding. The City does not admit the allegation, or
  any entitlement to overtime compensation, but to avoid the expense and
  burden of further litigation, the City Attorney’s Office recommended a
  settlement, in the amount of $85,000, coupled with an agreed-upon
  modification to Section 2.03 of the SMPOA MOU that will narrow the
  definition of “special event,” leave in place SMPOA’s ability to grieve and
  challenge a determination as to whether there has been a “special event”
  permitting overtime compensation for Lieutenants and Captains, provide
  discretion to the SMPD Chief, subject to budget constraints, to provide
  overtime compensation to Lieutenants and Captains under extraordinary
  circumstances that require the frequent scheduling of extra shifts over an
  extended period of time as a result of operational needs or as a result of an
  extended period of emergency, and place strict limits on SMPOA’s ability
  to grieve or challenge a determination by the SMPD Chief with respect to
  overtime compensation premised on extraordinary circumstances.

  Motion by Councilmember De la Torre, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem
  McCowan, to approve Settlement Agreement No. 11126 (CCS) in the
  amount of $85,000, with terms.

  2  December 29, 2020
 DocuSign Envelope ID: 03AEE48F-7A3E-4B58-A069-4BC128206EF7

  The motion was approved by the following vote:

  AYES:  Councilmembers De la Torre, Brock, McKeown, Davis, Parra,
  Mayor Pro Tem McCowan, Mayor Himmelrich
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

  1.D. Conference with Labor Negotiator: Government Code Section
  54957.6 --Agency Designated Representatives: Interim City Attorney
  George Cardona and Chief People Officer Lori Gentles; Bargaining
  Unit: Santa Monica Police Officers Association.

  The Interim City Attorney advised this matter was heard with Item 1.C.

  ADJOURNMENT  On order of the Mayor, the City Council meeting adjourned at 5:07 p.m.

  ATTEST:  APPROVED:

  Denise Anderson-Warren  Sue Himmelrich
  City Clerk  Mayor

  3  December 29, 2020
